snippet.title: "On a Sea of Glass" - TITANIC 113 Anniversary Livestream
snippet.description:
This year, I am pleased to invite Tad Fitch, J. Kent Layton, and Bill Wormstedt -- the historians and authors behind the books 'On a Sea of Glass: The Life & Loss of the RMS Titanic' and 'Recreating Titanic and Her Sisters: A Visual History' -- to team up with me yet again to commemorate, in real time, the anniversary of the Titanic disaster. We invite you to join us at 9:30pm EDT, 14-15 April 2024 on my YouTube Channel Part-Time Explorer when we go live. 

This year, we are honored to be joined by special guests Ken Marschall, renowned artist and the foremost visual historian of the Titanic and her sisters; Don Lynch, Titanic historian and author, and advisor on the James Cameron film Titanic; and Mark Chirnside, maritime and Olympic-class liner historian and author.

We have some exciting things in store for all those who join us: a brief update on the forthcoming HFX Studios' Lusitania experience "Lusitania: The Greyhound's Wake", as well as one on our upcoming book with the History Press titled "Lusitania: An Illustrated Biography".

It was some 12 years ago, in 2014, when I began a tradition of commemorating the sinking through these streams. Join us in real-time and pose questions that our panel will attempt to answer..

snippet.title: What Archaeologists Found at George Washington’s Mount Vernon Left Everyone Shocked
snippet.description: George Washington’s Mount Vernon stands as one of the most iconic historic estates in the United States. Located along the Potomac River in Virginia, it was the beloved home of America’s first president for more than 45 years. What began as a modest farmhouse inherited from his half brother grew under Washington’s direction into a grand mansion surrounded by sweeping gardens, working farms, and outbuildings that reflected both practicality and prestige. The estate wasn’t just a residence, it was a fully functioning plantation. Hundreds of people lived and labored on the property, maintaining the fields, livestock, and daily operations that sustained the estate and Washington’s wealth. So what did they discover there?

snippet.description:
One hundred years ago, Howard Carter made the greatest archaeological discovery of all time: the intact tomb of King Tutankhamun (KV62). But 33 centuries after his death, the Golden Pharaoh remains the most mysterious ruler in ancient Egyptian history. In this historical documentary, we bring together the world's leading Egyptologists, microbiologists, and digital engineers to decode the final secrets of Tutankhamun. Using cutting-edge CT scans and 3D laser imaging, we deconstruct the terrifying myths of the "Pharaoh's Curse," investigate the chemical anomaly that literally scorched his mummy inside the sarcophagus, and reveal how his legendary golden mask was actually stolen from a forgotten female pharaoh.

snippet.title: Albert Speer - Hitler’s Architect: Ambition, Power, and Guilt
snippet.description:
Albert Speer rose from ambitious architect to Hitler’s trusted confidant - but what was the real story behind the Third Reich’s “master builder”? Discover his controversial legacy here.

This video offers a compelling deep dive into the life and career of Albert Speer, exploring his meteoric rise within Nazi Germany and his complex relationship with Adolf Hitler. From his early days as a promising architecture student to becoming the chief architect of the Nazi party, Speer's designs transformed the look and feel of Nazi rallies and Berlin itself. Learn how Speer’s architectural vision, including the infamous Cathedral of Light and plans for the new Berlin, became central to Hitler’s propaganda and imperial ambitions.

As the war escalated, Speer was thrust into the role of Minister of Armaments, wielding unprecedented power over Germany’s war economy. The video examines his controversial use of forced labor, his centralization of production, and his navigation of Nazi politics, including his fraught relationship with rivals like Göring and Himmler. After the war, follow Speer’s journey from the Nuremberg Trials—where he accepted responsibility for Nazi crimes—to his years in Spandau Prison, secret writings, and eventual release. Through memoirs like Inside the Third Reich, Speer sought to shape his legacy, but questions linger about his true complicity and remorse. 

Whether you’re interested in World War II history, Nazi architecture, or the ethical dilemmas of power, this video unpacks the enigma of Albert Speer and his enduring impact on the historical record.

snippet.title: History's Weirdest War Tactics: Stink Bombs, Unsolved Mysteries, and Castro Plots
snippet.description:
Step into the world of bizarre wartime inventions, unsolved Soviet mysteries, and the wildest plots to kill Fidel Castro - this is history at its weirdest!

In this episode, we uncover the strangest weapons and covert operations of World War II, from the British SOE’s infamous fake poo bombs to top-secret stink liquids designed to demoralize the enemy. Discover how animal dung was weaponized to sabotage Nazi vehicles and learn about the real-life "Ministry for Ungentlemanly Warfare" - the origin of MI6's most unconventional tactics. Dive into the mad science behind the smelliest bombs ever devised, and find out why even the Americans tried to out-stink the Axis with their own secret formula, "Who Me?"

Next, journey to the frigid Ural Mountains and unravel the chilling, unsolved horror of the Dyatlov Pass incident. Ten hikers vanish on a snowy trek, leaving behind a tent slashed from the inside, bodies with mysterious injuries, radioactive traces, and a tangle of conspiracy theories involving avalanches, Yetis, UFOs, and Cold War cover-ups. Why did these prepared young adventurers flee into the night, barely clothed, never to return?

Finally, explore the almost cartoonish lengths the CIA went to in order to eliminate Cuba's Fidel Castro. From explosive cigars and poisoned wetsuits to LSD-sprayed TV studios and a mafia alliance, you'll hear the jaw-dropping details of 634 failed assassination attempts. Each plot is more outrageous than the last, highlighting the farcical side of Cold War espionage and the resilience of one of the 20th century’s most enigmatic leaders.

Packed with unbelievable stories, real-life mysteries, and dark humor, this video exposes just how strange history can get when the world goes to war and secret services are left to their own devices.

snippet.title: The Dramatic Sinking of SS Athenia
snippet.description:
On the evening of the 3rd September 1939, a British passenger liner buffeted its way through the North Atlantic, carrying over one thousand people; families, tourists and refugees homeward bound to North America. Only hours earlier, they had left a city spiralling into panic. Britain stood on the verge of declaring war on Germany. But it was a voyage Athenia would never finish - because waiting beneath the waves was a terrifying, deadly threat. The sinking of Athenia, the first to be caused by a U-Boat in WW2, caused outrage - not just among Britain and its allies but within the Nazi leadership. It’s loss is a story of high drama - but one which would be completely overshadowed by the sheer scale of loss caused by the Second World War.

A special 90 minute documentary about the aftermath of the Titanic from Nova Scotia's point of view - the terrible task of recovering the dead at the wrecksite and processing them, then burying those who were not claimed. 

When the Titanic slipped beneath the North Atlantic in the early hours of April 15, 1912, nearly 1,500 souls were lost. Although their lives were over, their stories were not. In the days that followed, a grim and solemn task began.

From Halifax, Nova Scotia, the cable ship Mackay-Bennett was among the first vessels sent to search the icy waters, tasked with recovering as many of the victims as possible. What the crew encountered was haunting—an endless expanse of debris, and the silent presence of those who had once filled the great liner’s decks. For the sailors, the work was difficult. For the undertakers and clergy waiting on shore, it was heartbreaking.

Halifax, Nova Scotia was the base of action for these dreaded expeditions. We’re looking in detail like never before at this chapter of the Titanic’s story, looking at rare artifacts, lost communication transcripts, and forgotten evidence to understand why Halifax was once called the City of the Dead. There, 150 victims remain to this day, buried beneath simple headstones, their names and stories still echoing across time.

This is the often-overlooked aftermath of the Titanic disaster—the story of those who carried out an unimaginable duty, and the city that became the final guardian of so many lost souls. This is Titanic’s Aftermath.

Featuring Charles Haas of the Titanic International Society, Dee Ryan-Meister of the Titanic Society of Atlantic Canada, as well as other local Nova Scotian historians including Blair Beed, Bob Chaulk, and Pat Teasdale.

snippet.description:
1940: Britain's vast fleet is tied down fighting German and Italian submarines and surface warships from the Atlantic to the Med. Carrying on the country's experience in crafting effective auxiliary cruisers, the Kriegsmarine deploys a 'first wave' of hunters disguised as harmless merchant vessels. The most deadly is known as 'Piguin'; her official designation is Ship 33, a converted merchantman which proves adept at bring ruin to Allied ships. Her skipper,  Ernst-Felix Kruder, is a gifted mine-layer who has big plans for the remote but important shipping channels of the south Australian coast. With Pinguin at hsi command and a choice crew, Kruder will lead his ship with ruthless efficiency - until a series of mistakes leads to his catastrophic downfall. It's one of the great maritime sagas of the second world war; this is the story of the raider 'Pinguin'.

snippet.title: The Brutal Reality of WWII: GIs in Italy and the Road to D-Day
snippet.description:
Experience the gritty reality of the Italian campaign and the build-up to D-Day through the eyes of Allied soldiers and commanders. Discover what it truly took to turn the tide of World War II.

This video dives deep into the hardships faced by GIs in Italy, from relentless weather and treacherous terrain to grueling battles against a determined enemy. You'll hear firsthand accounts of muddy foxholes, exhausting combat routines, and the critical importance of morale on the front lines. Learn how innovations in mine-clearing, intelligence gathering, and supply logistics shaped the campaign, and how every victory brought Allied forces one step closer to Berlin.

The narrative then shifts to the meticulous planning and massive preparations for Operation Overlord - the D-Day invasion. Explore the behind-the-scenes strategies, from constructing artificial harbors to training paratroopers and coordinating the largest amphibious assault in history. See how Allied leadership, including General Eisenhower and Prime Minister Churchill, motivated and prepared millions of troops for the decisive battle against Nazi Germany. Whether you’re a history buff or new to World War II, this video offers a vivid, human perspective on the cost, courage, and complexity behind some of the most pivotal moments of the war.

snippet.description:

It was one of the darkest days in American history. The city of Johnstown, Pennsylvania, was already flooded with 12 feet of rain water when the South Fork Dam, 14 miles up the valley, collapsed, unleashing a wall of water, up to 75 feet high and nearly 40 miles per hour. Nothing that stood in its way had a chance. Buildings were ripped from their foundations. Entire trains full of passengers were thrown like toys, and the City of Johnstown and its surrounding boroughs home to 30,000 people, were obliterated. 

What caused the dam collapse? Was it greed and negligence? Or was this terrible tragedy inevitable from the start? In this adventure, we’re traveling to Johnstown in Cambria County, Pennsylvania to see what little remains of the pre-flood city, and see the lasting impact that this disaster had on the town, and visiting the Johnstown Flood Museum to look at the artifacts that witnessed that terrible day in May, 1889.

Finally, we’re making our way to the dam itself, following the flood down the entirety of the valley, recreated with detailed animations to see the disaster like never before.

This is our biggest documentary yet and quite honestly, the hardest story we've covered. I had a hard time getting through some of the narrations with a stiff lip for this one.

snippet.title: Why This Great Lakes Lighthouse Story Remains Controversial After All These Years? | Fall Asleep To
snippet.description:
Great Lakes Lighthouses: The Most Controversial Story | Shipwreck, Unsolved Mysteries | Fall Asleep To

What drives a man to stand alone on a desolate rock, miles from the nearest soul, surrounded by a horizon that never changes and a silence that eventually begins to speak? For over two centuries, the Great Lakes have been guarded by these silent stone sentinels, but within their walls lie enigmas that the water refuses to wash away. Every Lighthouse story we uncover is a journey into the fragile boundary between human devotion and the deep, dark unknown.

Our journey begins at Gibraltar Point, the site of the region's oldest cold case. In 1815, keeper John Paul Radelmüller vanished into a winter night that left behind only questions and a lingering shadow. Though two individuals were accused of his tragic end, they walked free, leaving a jawbone found 78 years later as the only witness to his final moments. In the treacherous waters of the Great Lakes, few places evoke as much dread as Whitefish Point—the "Graveyard of the Inland Seas"—where a perfect 114-year record of guidance failed on the very night the SS Edmund Fitzgerald fought for its life in 1975.

The atmosphere thickens at Waugoshance, a "prison of waves" that later served as a target for top-secret naval operations. This Lighthouse story explores the baffling disappearance of John Herman, a man whose presence was reported by his assistant days after official records state he had already passed away on a distant island. If the keeper was no longer among the living, who was it that turned the key and locked the lantern room door?

As we navigate further, we encounter the prophetic riddle of Grand Island North. In 1908, a keeper sent a chilling letter home, predicting his own physical tragedy along the shoreline. Days later, he was found in a drifting boat with injuries that defied explanation, while his superior vanished into the wilderness forever. This Lighthouse story concludes at the desolate Pilot Island, now known as "Skeleton Island." It is a place where heroism and despair collided in the freezing surf, leaving behind a decaying monument to those who were pushed beyond the limits of human endurance.
Step into the shadows of history and explore these Great Lakes chronicles. Here, the beams of light do more than guide ships; they illuminate the secrets of those who stayed behind, and the mysteries that still echo when the wind is right.

The history of these towers is like an ancient, salt-stained ledger. Many of its pages have been torn out by the wind, and the ink that remains tells of a reality so isolating that the line between the living world and the echoes of the past becomes as thin as the morning mist.

But behind the success of his hit television show, a growing controversy was unfolding. Complaints, investigations, disciplinary hearings, and fierce criticism from fellow veterinarians raised questions that divided both the profession and the public. Was Dr. Pol an old-school vet unfairly targeted for his unconventional methods? Or were his critics exposing serious concerns that viewers never saw on screen? In this video, we take a closer look at the cases, court battles, and professional disputes that sparked one of the biggest controversies in veterinary television history.
